functions.name: botan_error_description
functions.signature: BOTAN_FFI_EXPORT(2, 8) const char* botan_error_description(int err);
functions.description: Converts a Botan FFI error code to a human-readable string. Useful for logging or diagnostics.
requirements: Argument err can be any integer; unknown codes return "Unknown error"

functions.name: botan_error_last_exception_message
functions.signature: BOTAN_FFI_EXPORT(3, 0) const char* botan_error_last_exception_message(void);
functions.description: Returns the message of the last exception caught in this thread by the Botan FFI. Pointer is transient and will be invalidated by the next Botan FFI call in the same thread.
requirements: Caller must copy the returned C-string to persistent storage before calling any other Botan FFI function in the same thread

functions.name: botan_ffi_api_version
functions.signature: BOTAN_FFI_EXPORT(2, 0) uint32_t botan_ffi_api_version(void);
functions.description: Returns the currently supported FFI API version as YYYYMMDD integer.

functions.name: botan_ffi_supports_api
functions.signature: BOTAN_FFI_EXPORT(2, 0) int botan_ffi_supports_api(uint32_t api_version);
functions.description: Checks whether the library supports the given FFI API version. Returns 0 if supported, negative otherwise.
requirements: api_version should typically be compared to botan_ffi_api_version() for compatibility checks

functions.name: botan_version_string
functions.signature: BOTAN_FFI_EXPORT(2, 0) const char* botan_version_string(void);
functions.description: Returns a free-form library version string, e.g., "2.0.0".

functions.name: botan_version_major
functions.signature: BOTAN_FFI_EXPORT(2, 0) uint32_t botan_version_major(void);
functions.description: Returns the library's major version.

functions.name: botan_version_minor
functions.signature: BOTAN_FFI_EXPORT(2, 0) uint32_t botan_version_minor(void);
functions.description: Returns the library's minor version.

functions.name: botan_version_patch
functions.signature: BOTAN_FFI_EXPORT(2, 0) uint32_t botan_version_patch(void);
functions.description: Returns the library's patch version.

functions.name: botan_version_datestamp
functions.signature: BOTAN_FFI_EXPORT(2, 0) uint32_t botan_version_datestamp(void);
functions.description: Returns the release date of this version as YYYYMMDD integer, or 0 if not an official release.

functions.name: botan_constant_time_compare
functions.signature: BOTAN_FFI_EXPORT(2, 3) int botan_constant_time_compare(const uint8_t* x, const uint8_t* y, size_t len);
functions.description: Constant-time compare of two byte arrays. Returns 0 if equal, -1 otherwise.
requirements: x and y must point to at least len bytes
All pointers must be non-NULL unless len is 0 (then x and y may be NULL)

functions.name: botan_same_mem
functions.signature:
BOTAN_FFI_DEPRECATED("Use botan_constant_time_compare")
BOTAN_FFI_EXPORT(2, 0) int botan_same_mem(const uint8_t* x, const uint8_t* y, size_t len);
functions.description: Deprecated constant-time memory comparison. Use botan_constant_time_compare instead.
requirements: x and y must point to at least len bytes
Prefer botan_constant_time_compare

functions.name: botan_scrub_mem
functions.signature: BOTAN_FFI_EXPORT(2, 2) int botan_scrub_mem(void* mem, size_t bytes);
functions.description: Securely zeroizes a memory region to prevent compiler elision.
requirements: mem must point to at least bytes writable bytes; bytes may be zero
Use only for memory you own and intend to wipe

functions.name: botan_hex_encode
functions.signature: BOTAN_FFI_EXPORT(2, 0) int botan_hex_encode(const uint8_t* x, size_t len, char* out, uint32_t flags);
functions.description: Encodes binary data to hexadecimal ASCII.
requirements: x must point to at least len bytes (or may be NULL if len == 0)
out must point to a buffer of at least 2*len bytes
flags may be 0 or BOTAN_FFI_HEX_LOWER_CASE to select case

functions.name: botan_hex_decode
functions.signature: BOTAN_FFI_EXPORT(2, 3) int botan_hex_decode(const char* hex_str, size_t in_len, uint8_t* out, size_t* out_len);
functions.description: Decodes a hex string (ignores whitespace) into bytes.
requirements: hex_str must point to at least in_len chars (or be NULL if in_len == 0)
out_len must be non-NULL; on input contains output buffer size; on success set to bytes written
out must have at least floor(in_len/2) bytes; if too small returns error and sets required size

functions.name: botan_base64_encode
functions.signature: BOTAN_FFI_EXPORT(2, 3) int botan_base64_encode(const uint8_t* x, size_t len, char* out, size_t* out_len);
functions.description: Base64-encodes input bytes into out.
requirements: x must point to at least len bytes (or may be NULL if len == 0)
out_len must be non-NULL; on input size of out; on success set to bytes written
out must be large enough; if insufficient, function returns error and sets required size

functions.name: botan_base64_decode
functions.signature: BOTAN_FFI_EXPORT(2, 3) int botan_base64_decode(const char* base64_str, size_t in_len, uint8_t* out, size_t* out_len);
functions.description: Decodes base64 string into bytes.
requirements: base64_str must point to at least in_len chars (or be NULL if in_len == 0)
out_len must be non-NULL; on input size of out; on success set to bytes written
If out is too small, returns error and sets required size

functions.name: botan_rng_init
functions.signature: BOTAN_FFI_EXPORT(2, 0) int botan_rng_init(botan_rng_t* rng, const char* rng_type);
functions.description: Creates a Botan RNG of the given type (e.g., "system", "esdm-full", "user", ...).
requirements: rng must be non-NULL and will receive the created RNG handle
rng_type may be NULL to choose a default; otherwise must be a known type string

functions.name: botan_rng_init_custom
functions.signature:
BOTAN_FFI_EXPORT(3, 0)
int botan_rng_init_custom(botan_rng_t* rng_out,
                          const char* rng_name,
                          void* context,
                          int (*get_cb)(void* context, uint8_t* out, size_t out_len),
                          int (*add_entropy_cb)(void* context, const uint8_t input[], size_t length),
                          void (*destroy_cb)(void* context));
functions.description: Initializes a custom RNG using application-provided callbacks for random byte generation, optional entropy addition, and destruction.
requirements: rng_out must be non-NULL
get_cb must be non-NULL and return 0 on success
add_entropy_cb and destroy_cb may be NULL
rng_name is an application-defined identifier (may be NULL)
Callbacks must be thread-safe if RNG is used concurrently by the application

functions.name: botan_rng_get
functions.signature: BOTAN_FFI_EXPORT(2, 0) int botan_rng_get(botan_rng_t rng, uint8_t* out, size_t out_len);
functions.description: Fills out with out_len random bytes from the RNG.
requirements: rng must be a valid initialized RNG handle
out must point to at least out_len writable bytes

functions.name: botan_system_rng_get
functions.signature: BOTAN_FFI_EXPORT(3, 0) int botan_system_rng_get(uint8_t* out, size_t out_len);
functions.description: Obtains random bytes directly from the system RNG.
requirements: out must point to at least out_len writable bytes

functions.name: botan_rng_reseed
functions.signature: BOTAN_FFI_EXPORT(2, 0) int botan_rng_reseed(botan_rng_t rng, size_t bits);
functions.description: Reseeds the RNG from the system RNG with approximately the requested number of entropy bits.
requirements: rng must be a valid initialized RNG handle
bits specifies the target reseed entropy; must be a reasonable positive value (implementation-defined)

functions.name: botan_rng_reseed_from_rng
functions.signature: BOTAN_FFI_EXPORT(2, 8) int botan_rng_reseed_from_rng(botan_rng_t rng, botan_rng_t source_rng, size_t bits);
functions.description: Reseeds rng by drawing entropy from another RNG handle.
requirements: rng and source_rng must be valid initialized RNG handles
bits specifies desired entropy amount; should be positive

functions.name: botan_rng_add_entropy
functions.signature: BOTAN_FFI_EXPORT(2, 8) int botan_rng_add_entropy(botan_rng_t rng, const uint8_t* entropy, size_t entropy_len);
functions.description: Adds application-provided seed material to the RNG.
requirements: rng must be valid
entropy must point to at least entropy_len bytes (or may be NULL if entropy_len == 0)

functions.name: botan_rng_destroy
functions.signature: BOTAN_FFI_EXPORT(2, 0) int botan_rng_destroy(botan_rng_t rng);
functions.description: Destroys an RNG and frees associated resources.
requirements: rng must be a valid RNG handle or NULL; returns error if invalid object handle

functions.name: botan_hash_init
functions.signature: BOTAN_FFI_EXPORT(2, 0) int botan_hash_init(botan_hash_t* hash, const char* hash_name, uint32_t flags);
functions.description: Creates a hash function instance by name (e.g., "SHA-384").
requirements: hash must be non-NULL
hash_name must name a supported hash algorithm
flags must be 0 in current API; other values return BOTAN_FFI_ERROR_BAD_FLAG

functions.name: botan_hash_copy_state
functions.signature: BOTAN_FFI_EXPORT(2, 2) int botan_hash_copy_state(botan_hash_t* dest, botan_hash_t source);
functions.description: Clones the internal state of a hash instance into a new hash object.
requirements: dest must be non-NULL
source must be a valid hash handle

functions.name: botan_hash_output_length
functions.signature: BOTAN_FFI_EXPORT(2, 0) int botan_hash_output_length(botan_hash_t hash, size_t* output_length);
functions.description: Retrieves the output length (in bytes) of the hash function.
requirements: hash must be valid
output_length must be non-NULL

functions.name: botan_hash_block_size
functions.signature: BOTAN_FFI_EXPORT(2, 2) int botan_hash_block_size(botan_hash_t hash, size_t* block_size);
functions.description: Retrieves the internal block size (in bytes) of the hash function.
requirements: hash must be valid
block_size must be non-NULL

functions.name: botan_hash_update
functions.signature: BOTAN_FFI_EXPORT(2, 0) int botan_hash_update(botan_hash_t hash, const uint8_t* in, size_t in_len);
functions.description: Feeds input bytes to the hash function.
requirements: hash must be valid
in must point to at least in_len bytes (or may be NULL if in_len == 0)

functions.name: botan_hash_final
functions.signature: BOTAN_FFI_EXPORT(2, 0) int botan_hash_final(botan_hash_t hash, uint8_t out[]);
functions.description: Finalizes the hash computation, writes digest of botan_hash_output_length() bytes to out, then resets for a new computation.
requirements: hash must be valid
out must point to at least botan_hash_output_length() writable bytes

functions.name: botan_hash_clear
functions.signature: BOTAN_FFI_EXPORT(2, 0) int botan_hash_clear(botan_hash_t hash);
functions.description: Resets the hash state to begin a new digest computation.
requirements: hash must be valid

functions.name: botan_hash_destroy
functions.signature: BOTAN_FFI_EXPORT(2, 0) int botan_hash_destroy(botan_hash_t hash);
functions.description: Destroys a hash object and frees its resources.
requirements: hash must be a valid handle or NULL; invalid object handle returns error

functions.name: botan_hash_name
functions.signature: BOTAN_FFI_EXPORT(2, 8) int botan_hash_name(botan_hash_t hash, char* name, size_t* name_len);
functions.description: Retrieves the algorithm name of the hash instance.
requirements: hash must be valid
name_len must be non-NULL; on input size of name; on success set to bytes written
If name buffer is too small, function returns error and sets required size

functions.name: botan_mac_init
functions.signature: BOTAN_FFI_EXPORT(2, 0) int botan_mac_init(botan_mac_t* mac, const char* mac_name, uint32_t flags);
functions.description: Creates a MAC instance by name (e.g., "HMAC(SHA-384)").
requirements: mac must be non-NULL
mac_name must name a supported MAC
flags must be 0; other values return an error

functions.name: botan_mac_output_length
functions.signature: BOTAN_FFI_EXPORT(2, 0) int botan_mac_output_length(botan_mac_t mac, size_t* output_length);
functions.description: Retrieves the MAC output length in bytes.
requirements: mac must be valid
output_length must be non-NULL

functions.name: botan_mac_set_key
functions.signature: BOTAN_FFI_EXPORT(2, 0) int botan_mac_set_key(botan_mac_t mac, const uint8_t* key, size_t key_len);
functions.description: Sets the key for the MAC.
requirements: mac must be valid
key must point to at least key_len bytes (or may be NULL if key_len == 0, if allowed by MAC)
Key length must be within the MAC's supported key size range

functions.name: botan_mac_set_nonce
functions.signature: BOTAN_FFI_EXPORT(3, 0) int botan_mac_set_nonce(botan_mac_t mac, const uint8_t* nonce, size_t nonce_len);
functions.description: Optionally sets a nonce for MACs that support nonces.
requirements: mac must be valid
nonce must point to at least nonce_len bytes (or may be NULL if nonce_len == 0)
Only valid for MACs that support nonces; otherwise returns error

functions.name: botan_mac_update
functions.signature: BOTAN_FFI_EXPORT(2, 0) int botan_mac_update(botan_mac_t mac, const uint8_t* buf, size_t len);
functions.description: Feeds input bytes to the MAC.
requirements: mac must be valid and keyed (botan_mac_set_key must have been called)
buf must point to at least len bytes (or may be NULL if len == 0)

functions.name: botan_mac_final
functions.signature: BOTAN_FFI_EXPORT(2, 0) int botan_mac_final(botan_mac_t mac, uint8_t out[]);
functions.description: Finalizes the MAC computation, writes botan_mac_output_length() bytes to out, then resets for a new computation.
requirements: mac must be valid and keyed
out must point to at least botan_mac_output_length() writable bytes

functions.name: botan_mac_clear
functions.signature: BOTAN_FFI_EXPORT(2, 0) int botan_mac_clear(botan_mac_t mac);
functions.description: Clears the MAC state (but not the key), enabling a new computation.
requirements: mac must be valid

functions.name: botan_mac_name
functions.signature: BOTAN_FFI_EXPORT(2, 8) int botan_mac_name(botan_mac_t mac, char* name, size_t* name_len);
functions.description: Retrieves the algorithm name of the MAC instance.
requirements: mac must be valid
name_len must be non-NULL; on input capacity of name; on success set to bytes written
If name is too small, returns error and sets required size

functions.name: botan_mac_get_keyspec
functions.signature:
BOTAN_FFI_EXPORT(2, 8)
int botan_mac_get_keyspec(botan_mac_t mac,
                          size_t* out_minimum_keylength,
                          size_t* out_maximum_keylength,
                          size_t* out_keylength_modulo);
functions.description: Retrieves the MAC's key length constraints: min, max, and modulo alignment.
requirements: mac must be valid
Any of out_minimum_keylength, out_maximum_keylength, out_keylength_modulo may be NULL to ignore that output

functions.name: botan_mac_destroy
functions.signature: BOTAN_FFI_EXPORT(2, 0) int botan_mac_destroy(botan_mac_t mac);
functions.description: Destroys a MAC object and frees resources.
requirements: mac must be a valid handle or NULL; invalid object handle returns error

functions.name: botan_cipher_init
functions.signature: BOTAN_FFI_EXPORT(2, 0) int botan_cipher_init(botan_cipher_t* cipher, const char* name, uint32_t flags);
functions.description: Initializes a cipher mode object by algorithm name and flags indicating encrypt/decrypt direction.
requirements: cipher must be non-NULL
name must be a valid cipher mode spec (e.g., "AES-256/GCM")
flags direction must be BOTAN_CIPHER_INIT_FLAG_ENCRYPT or BOTAN_CIPHER_INIT_FLAG_DECRYPT; other bits are reserved

functions.name: botan_cipher_name
functions.signature: BOTAN_FFI_EXPORT(2, 8) int botan_cipher_name(botan_cipher_t cipher, char* name, size_t* name_len);
functions.description: Returns the canonical name of the cipher mode.
requirements: cipher must be valid
name_len must be non-NULL; on input buffer size; on success bytes written
If buffer too small, returns error and sets required size

functions.name: botan_cipher_output_length
functions.signature: BOTAN_FFI_EXPORT(2, 8) int botan_cipher_output_length(botan_cipher_t cipher, size_t in_len, size_t* out_len);
functions.description: Computes the output length for a given input size for this cipher mode.
requirements: cipher must be valid
out_len must be non-NULL

functions.name: botan_cipher_valid_nonce_length
functions.signature: BOTAN_FFI_EXPORT(2, 0) int botan_cipher_valid_nonce_length(botan_cipher_t cipher, size_t nl);
functions.description: Returns 1 if the given nonce length is valid for this cipher; 0 if invalid; negative on error.
requirements: cipher must be valid

functions.name: botan_cipher_get_tag_length
functions.signature: BOTAN_FFI_EXPORT(2, 0) int botan_cipher_get_tag_length(botan_cipher_t cipher, size_t* tag_size);
functions.description: Gets the tag length in bytes for AEAD ciphers; 0 for non-AEAD modes.
requirements: cipher must be valid
tag_size must be non-NULL

functions.name: botan_cipher_is_authenticated
functions.signature: BOTAN_FFI_EXPORT(3, 3) int botan_cipher_is_authenticated(botan_cipher_t cipher);
functions.description: Returns 1 if cipher is an AEAD (authenticated) mode; 0 otherwise; negative on error.
requirements: cipher must be valid

functions.name: botan_cipher_requires_entire_message
functions.signature: BOTAN_FFI_EXPORT(3, 4) int botan_cipher_requires_entire_message(botan_cipher_t cipher);
functions.description: Returns 1 if the cipher requires the full message before producing output; 0 otherwise; negative on error.
requirements: cipher must be valid

functions.name: botan_cipher_get_default_nonce_length
functions.signature: BOTAN_FFI_EXPORT(2, 0) int botan_cipher_get_default_nonce_length(botan_cipher_t cipher, size_t* nl);
functions.description: Returns the default nonce length for the cipher mode.
requirements: cipher must be valid
nl must be non-NULL

functions.name: botan_cipher_get_update_granularity
functions.signature: BOTAN_FFI_EXPORT(2, 0) int botan_cipher_get_update_granularity(botan_cipher_t cipher, size_t* ug);
functions.description: Returns the minimum input size granularity required by botan_cipher_update when not finalizing.
requirements: cipher must be valid
ug must be non-NULL

functions.name: botan_cipher_get_ideal_update_granularity
functions.signature: BOTAN_FFI_EXPORT(3, 0) int botan_cipher_get_ideal_update_granularity(botan_cipher_t cipher, size_t* ug);
functions.description: Returns an ideal (larger) update granularity for performance tuning.
requirements: cipher must be valid
ug must be non-NULL

functions.name: botan_cipher_query_keylen
functions.signature:
BOTAN_FFI_EXPORT(2, 0)
int botan_cipher_query_keylen(botan_cipher_t cipher, size_t* out_minimum_keylength, size_t* out_maximum_keylength);
functions.description: Returns legacy min/max key length information. Prefer botan_cipher_get_keyspec.
requirements: cipher must be valid
out_minimum_keylength and/or out_maximum_keylength may be NULL

functions.name: botan_cipher_get_keyspec
functions.signature:
BOTAN_FFI_EXPORT(2, 8)
int botan_cipher_get_keyspec(botan_cipher_t cipher, size_t* min_keylen, size_t* max_keylen, size_t* mod_keylen);
functions.description: Returns the cipher's supported key length range and modulo alignment.
requirements: cipher must be valid
Any of min_keylen, max_keylen, mod_keylen may be NULL

functions.name: botan_cipher_set_key
functions.signature: BOTAN_FFI_EXPORT(2, 0) int botan_cipher_set_key(botan_cipher_t cipher, const uint8_t* key, size_t key_len);
functions.description: Sets the key for the cipher mode.
requirements: cipher must be valid
key must point to at least key_len bytes
key_len must satisfy botan_cipher_get_keyspec constraints

functions.name: botan_cipher_reset
functions.signature: BOTAN_FFI_EXPORT(2, 8) int botan_cipher_reset(botan_cipher_t cipher);
functions.description: Resets per-message state (nonce, associated data, processed data) without changing the key.
requirements: cipher must be valid

functions.name: botan_cipher_set_associated_data
functions.signature: BOTAN_FFI_EXPORT(2, 0) int botan_cipher_set_associated_data(botan_cipher_t cipher, const uint8_t* ad, size_t ad_len);
functions.description: Sets Additional Authenticated Data for AEAD modes. Fails for non-AEAD.
requirements: cipher must be valid and AEAD-capable
ad must point to at least ad_len bytes (or may be NULL if ad_len == 0)
Must be called before botan_cipher_start for AEAD modes

functions.name: botan_cipher_start
functions.signature: BOTAN_FFI_EXPORT(2, 0) int botan_cipher_start(botan_cipher_t cipher, const uint8_t* nonce, size_t nonce_len);
functions.description: Begins processing a new message with the given nonce.
requirements: cipher must be valid and keyed
nonce must be provided with a supported length for this cipher (use botan_cipher_valid_nonce_length)
Must be called before botan_cipher_update

functions.name: botan_cipher_update
functions.signature:
BOTAN_FFI_EXPORT(2, 0)
int botan_cipher_update(botan_cipher_t cipher,
                        uint32_t flags,
                        uint8_t output[],
                        size_t output_size,
                        size_t* output_written,
                        const uint8_t input_bytes[],

import random
import string
from typing import List

def _rand_whitespace(r: random.Random) -> str:
    # Common ASCII whitespace that hex decoders often skip
    ws = [' ', '\t', '\n', '\r']
    return ''.join(r.choice(ws) for _ in range(r.randint(0, 3)))

def _chunked_hex(r: random.Random, nbytes: int, with_ws: bool, case: str) -> str:
    # Generate nbytes of random data and encode as hex with optional whitespace/grouping
    data = bytes(r.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(nbytes))
    hexchars = data.hex()
    if case == 'upper':
        hexchars = hexchars.upper()
    elif case == 'mixed':
        # Randomize case per nibble
        tmp = []
        for ch in hexchars:
            if ch in 'abcdef' and r.random() < 0.5:
                tmp.append(ch.upper())
            else:
                tmp.append(ch)
        hexchars = ''.join(tmp)

    if not with_ws:
        return hexchars

    # Insert random whitespace separators at random positions and group sizes
    out = []
    i = 0
    while i < len(hexchars):
        group = r.randint(1, 8)  # group by 1..8 nibbles
        out.append(hexchars[i:i+group])
        i += group
        if i < len(hexchars) and r.random() < 0.6:
            out.append(_rand_whitespace(r))
    # Also occasionally add leading/trailing whitespace
    prefix = _rand_whitespace(r) if r.random() < 0.5 else ''
    suffix = _rand_whitespace(r) if r.random() < 0.5 else ''
    return prefix + ''.join(out) + suffix

def _odd_length_hex(r: random.Random, target_nibbles: int, with_ws: bool) -> str:
    # Ensure odd number of hex digits; decoder may treat as error or handle len-1
    nibbles = target_nibbles if target_nibbles % 2 == 1 else max(1, target_nibbles - 1)
    # fill with valid hex digits
    digits = ''.join(r.choice('0123456789abcdef') for _ in range(nibbles))
    if r.random() < 0.5:
        digits = digits.upper()
    if with_ws and r.random() < 0.8:
        # sprinkle whitespace
        out = []
        for ch in digits:
            out.append(ch)
            if r.random() < 0.2:
                out.append(_rand_whitespace(r))
        return ''.join(out)
    return digits

def _invalid_char_hex(r: random.Random, length: int, with_ws: bool) -> str:
    # Mix valid hex with some invalid characters to trigger error handling paths
    valid = '0123456789abcdef'
    invalid = ''.join(ch for ch in string.printable if ch not in valid and ch.upper() not in 'ABCDEF' and ch not in '\x0b\x0c')
    out = []
    for _ in range(length):
        if r.random() < 0.8:
            ch = r.choice(valid)
            if r.random() < 0.5:
                ch = ch.upper()
            out.append(ch)
        else:
            out.append(r.choice(invalid))
        if with_ws and r.random() < 0.15:
            out.append(_rand_whitespace(r))
    # maybe lead/trail ws
    if with_ws and r.random() < 0.5:
        out.insert(0, _rand_whitespace(r))
    if with_ws and r.random() < 0.5:
        out.append(_rand_whitespace(r))
    return ''.join(out)

def _edge_case_hex(r: random.Random) -> str:
    # Handcrafted interesting edge cases
    cases = [
        '',
        '00',
        'FF',
        'ff',
        '0',  # odd length
        'F',  # odd length upper
        '000102030405060708090A0B0C0D0E0F',
        'deadbeef',
        'DEADBEEF',
        'CafeBabe',
        'cafebabe',
        'AB CD EF',
        'ab\ncd\ref\t01',
        '  \t\n',
        '1234567890ABCDEF'*4,  # longer but within 1024
        'a'*1023,  # 1023 nibbles -> odd length large
    ]
    return r.choice(cases)

def _bounded_length(r: random.Random, min_len: int, max_len: int) -> int:
    # Bias toward boundaries and small sizes
    choices = [min_len, min_len+1, max_len, max_len-1]
    if max_len - min_len > 4:
        choices += [r.randint(min_len, max_len) for _ in range(6)]
    return r.choice(choices)

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed)

    # Decide scenario covering various decoder behaviors
    scenario = r.choices(
        population=['valid_ws', 'valid_clean', 'odd_len', 'invalid_chars', 'edge_case'],
        weights=[30, 25, 15, 15, 15],
        k=1
    )[0]

    # Ensure we respect the fuzzer cap of 1024 bytes for the string argument
    # We'll generate up to 1024 characters (not bytes), since it will be passed as std::string
    max_chars = 1024

    if scenario == 'valid_ws':
        # Valid hex with whitespace groupings
        # Choose total decoded length in bytes biased to boundaries
        nbytes = _bounded_length(r, 0, max_chars // 2)
        case = r.choice(['lower', 'upper', 'mixed'])
        s = _chunked_hex(r, nbytes, with_ws=True, case=case)
        s = s[:max_chars]
    elif scenario == 'valid_clean':
        nbytes = _bounded_length(r, 0, max_chars // 2)
        case = r.choice(['lower', 'upper', 'mixed'])
        s = _chunked_hex(r, nbytes, with_ws=False, case=case)
    elif scenario == 'odd_len':
        # Odd number of hex digits, possibly with whitespace
        target_nibbles = _bounded_length(r, 1, max_chars)
        s = _odd_length_hex(r, target_nibbles, with_ws=r.random() < 0.7)
        s = s[:max_chars]
    elif scenario == 'invalid_chars':
        length = _bounded_length(r, 1, max_chars)
        s = _invalid_char_hex(r, length, with_ws=r.random() < 0.7)

    else:  # edge_case
        s = _edge_case_hex(r)
        if len(s) > max_chars:
            s = s[:max_chars]

    return s.encode('ascii', errors='strict')

import random
import string
from typing import List

# Generator for interesting Base64 strings for botan_base64_decode fuzzer
# - Include valid/invalid cases, varied padding, whitespace, URL-safe variants, short/long lengths
# - Keep output <= 4096 bytes

_B64_STD = "ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789+/"
_B64_URL = "ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789-_"
_WS = ["\r", "\n", "\t", " "]

def _chunk(s: str, n: int) -> str:
    return "".join(s[i:i+n] + ("\n" if i + n < len(s) else "") for i in range(0, len(s), n))

def _rand_bytes(rng: random.Random, n: int) -> bytes:
    return bytes(rng.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(n))

def _b64_encode_bytes(data: bytes, alphabet: str) -> str:
    # Manual base64 encode to allow switching alphabets
    out = []
    pad_char = '='
    for i in range(0, len(data), 3):
        block = data[i:i+3]
        b = int.from_bytes(block.ljust(3, b"\x00"), 'big')
        pad = 3 - len(block)
        # 4 sextets
        s1 = (b >> 18) & 0x3F
        s2 = (b >> 12) & 0x3F
        s3 = (b >> 6) & 0x3F
        s4 = b & 0x3F
        out.append(alphabet[s1])
        out.append(alphabet[s2])
        out.append(alphabet[s3] if pad < 2 else pad_char)
        out.append(alphabet[s4] if pad < 1 else pad_char)
    return "".join(out)

def _insert_whitespace(rng: random.Random, s: str) -> str:
    # Randomly insert whitespace every few chars
    if not s:
        return s
    pieces: List[str] = []
    for ch in s:
        pieces.append(ch)
        if rng.random() < 0.06:
            pieces.append(rng.choice(_WS))
    # Maybe add leading/trailing whitespace
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        pieces.insert(0, rng.choice(_WS) * rng.randint(1, 3))
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        pieces.append(rng.choice(_WS) * rng.randint(1, 3))
    return "".join(pieces)

def _make_valid_std_b64(rng: random.Random, max_len: int) -> str:
    # Choose a target decoded length
    decoded_len = rng.randint(0, min(1024, max(0, max_len // 1)))
    raw = _rand_bytes(rng, decoded_len)
    s = _b64_encode_bytes(raw, _B64_STD)
    # Optional line breaks at 64 or 76
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        width = rng.choice([64, 76])
        s = _chunk(s, width)
    # Optional whitespace sprinkling
    if rng.random() < 0.7:
        s = _insert_whitespace(rng, s)
    return s

def _make_valid_url_b64(rng: random.Random, max_len: int) -> str:
    decoded_len = rng.randint(0, min(1024, max(0, max_len // 1)))
    raw = _rand_bytes(rng, decoded_len)
    s = _b64_encode_bytes(raw, _B64_URL)
    # URL-safe often omits padding; randomly drop it
    if rng.random() < 0.7:
        s = s.rstrip('=')
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        s = _insert_whitespace(rng, s)
    return s

def _make_edge_padding(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Construct strings that exercise 1 or 2 padding chars and boundary lengths
    k = rng.choice([1, 2])
    # Create data length mod 3 equals 1 -> '==' or equals 2 -> '='
    if k == 2:
        raw_len = rng.randrange(1, 200) * 3 + 1
    else:
        raw_len = rng.randrange(1, 200) * 3 + 2
    raw = _rand_bytes(rng, raw_len)
    return _b64_encode_bytes(raw, _B64_STD)

def _make_invalid_chars(rng: random.Random, max_len: int) -> str:
    # Mostly valid base64 but with occasional invalid characters
    length = rng.randint(8, min(1024, max(8, max_len)))
    valid = _B64_STD
    invalid_pool = ''.join(sorted(set(string.printable) - set(valid + '=' + ''.join(_WS))))
    s = []
    for i in range(length):
        if rng.random() < 0.1:
            s.append(rng.choice(invalid_pool))
        else:
            s.append(rng.choice(valid + '='))
    # Optionally inject whitespace
    if rng.random() < 0.7:
        s = list(_insert_whitespace(rng, ''.join(s)))
    return ''.join(s)

def _make_tricky_lengths(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Create lengths around multiples of 4, with/without padding
    base_len = rng.choice([0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 7, 8, 15, 16, 31, 32, 63, 64, 127, 128, 255, 256])
    alphabet = rng.choice([_B64_STD, _B64_URL])
    s = ''.join(alphabet[rng.randrange(64)] for _ in range(base_len))
    # Optionally add padding chars regardless of alignment
    if rng.random() < 0.6:
        s += '=' * rng.randrange(0, 3)
    # Sprinkle whitespace
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        s = _insert_whitespace(rng, s)
    return s

def _catalog(rng: random.Random, budget: int) -> List[str]:
    gens = [
        lambda: _make_valid_std_b64(rng, budget),
        lambda: _make_valid_url_b64(rng, budget),
        lambda: _make_edge_padding(rng),
        lambda: _make_invalid_chars(rng, budget),
        lambda: _make_tricky_lengths(rng),
        lambda: "",  # empty input
        lambda: "=",  # lonely padding
        lambda: "====",  # many paddings
        lambda: "\n\r\n",  # whitespace-only
    ]
    # Weighted choice to bias toward valid inputs but still include invalid
    weights = [5, 3, 3, 2, 2, 1, 1, 1, 1]
    choice = rng.choices(gens, weights=weights, k=1)[0]
    return [choice()]

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    # Maximum allowed by stub before resize is 1024, keep well under global 4096 cap
    max_total = 1024
    pieces = _catalog(rng, max_total)

    s = pieces[0]

    # Final clamp and ensure ASCII bytes
    if len(s) > max_total:
        s = s[:max_total]
    return s.encode('ascii', errors='ignore')

from typing import List

def _rand_ascii(rng: random.Random, min_len: int, max_len: int) -> str:
    length = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    alphabet = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + string.punctuation + ' '
    return ''.join(rng.choice(alphabet) for _ in range(length))

def _rand_utf8(rng: random.Random, min_len: int, max_len: int) -> str:
    length = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    # A mix of BMP and some multi-byte sequences
    blocks = [
        (0x0020, 0x007E),   # printable ASCII
        (0x00A1, 0x017F),   # Latin-1 supplement + extended
        (0x0391, 0x03C9),   # Greek
        (0x0400, 0x04FF),   # Cyrillic
        (0x2000, 0x206F),   # General punctuation
        (0x2190, 0x21FF),   # Arrows
        (0x2600, 0x26FF),   # Misc symbols
        (0x4E00, 0x9FFF),   # CJK Unified Ideographs (sample)
    ]
    s = []
    for _ in range(length):
        lo, hi = rng.choice(blocks)
        cp = rng.randint(lo, hi)
        # Avoid surrogate range
        if 0xD800 <= cp <= 0xDFFF:
            cp = 0x20
        s.append(chr(cp))
    return ''.join(s)

def _rand_binary_like(rng: random.Random, min_len: int, max_len: int) -> bytes:
    length = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    # Include NULs to test explicit length paths
    return bytes(rng.randrange(0, 256) for _ in range(length))

def _bcrypt_passwords(rng: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    # Bcrypt typically treats passwords up to 72 bytes; include boundary cases.
    samples = [
        '',
        'a',
        'password',
        'P@ssw0rd!',
        ' ' * 8,
        '😀' * 10,  # multibyte
        'x' * 72,
        'x' * 73,
    ]
    # Add random ascii/utf8 variants
    samples.append(_rand_ascii(rng, 1, 40))
    samples.append(_rand_utf8(rng, 1, 40))
    return samples

def _pbkdf_passwords(rng: random.Random) -> List[bytes]:
    # Include empty, short, long, binary-with-NUL, and typical passphrases
    out: List[bytes] = []
    out.append(b'')
    out.append(b'pass')
    out.append(b'correct horse battery staple')
    out.append(_rand_ascii(rng, 5, 60).encode('utf-8', 'ignore'))
    out.append(_rand_utf8(rng, 5, 60).encode('utf-8'))
    out.append(_rand_binary_like(rng, 8, 80))
    # Include embedded NUL explicitly
    b = bytearray(_rand_ascii(rng, 5, 20).encode('utf-8'))
    if b:
        b.insert(rng.randrange(0, len(b)+1), 0)
    out.append(bytes(b))
    return out

def _salt_variants(rng: random.Random) -> List[bytes]:
    # Salts up to 64 bytes (per stub truncation), include empty and various sizes
    salts: List[bytes] = [
        b'',
        b'NaCl',
        os.urandom(rng.randint(4, 16)),
        os.urandom(32),
        os.urandom(64),
    ]
    # Include repetitive and low-entropy salts
    salts.append(b'\x00' * 16)
    salts.append(b'A' * 64)
    return salts

def _bcrypt_hash_samples(rng: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    # Valid-looking bcrypt hashes and malformed ones to exercise validators
    valid_cost = rng.randint(4, 12)
    # 22-char Base64-ish salt and 31-char hash body; placeholders are fine
    def rbase64(n: int) -> str:
        alphabet = './' + string.ascii_letters + string.digits
        return ''.join(rng.choice(alphabet) for _ in range(n))
    samples = [
        f"$2b${valid_cost:02d}${rbase64(22)}{rbase64(31)}",
        f"$2a${valid_cost:02d}${rbase64(22)}{rbase64(31)}",
        f"$2y${valid_cost:02d}${rbase64(22)}{rbase64(31)}",
        '',  # empty -> invalid path
        'not_a_hash',
        '$2b$05$short',
    ]
    return samples

def _srp_fields(rng: random.Random) -> List[bytes]:
    # Identifiers and salts used by SRP-related fuzzers; strings are fine
    ids = [b'user', b'admin', _rand_ascii(rng, 1, 12).encode(), _rand_utf8(rng, 1, 12).encode()]
    salts = _salt_variants(rng)
    Bs = []
    # B public value sized 32..512 bytes; ensure non-empty
    for _ in range(3):
        size = rng.randint(32, 128)
        Bs.append(os.urandom(size))
    return ids + salts + Bs

def _assemble_corpus(rng: random.Random) -> List[bytes]:
    corpus: List[bytes] = []

    # Password strings for FUZZ_PARAM_STR consumers (PBKDF, pwdhash, bcrypt, SRP)
    for s in _bcrypt_passwords(rng):
        corpus.append(s.encode('utf-8', 'ignore'))

    for p in _pbkdf_passwords(rng):
        corpus.append(p)

    # Salts (for PBKDF, scrypt, SRP)
    corpus.extend(_salt_variants(rng))

    # Bcrypt hash strings for botan_bcrypt_is_valid
    for h in _bcrypt_hash_samples(rng):
        corpus.append(h.encode('ascii', 'ignore'))

    # SRP fields and B values
    corpus.extend(_srp_fields(rng))

    # Ensure diversity: include some PEM/DER-like blobs for privkey loader
    pem = (
        "-----BEGIN PRIVATE KEY-----\n" +
        "MIIBVwIBADANBgkqhkiG9w0BAQEFAASCAT8wggE7AgEAAkEAu8s1\n" +
        "-----END PRIVATE KEY-----\n"
    ).encode('ascii')
    der_prefix = b"\x30\x82" + bytes([rng.randint(0, 3), rng.randint(0, 255)]) + os.urandom(rng.randint(20, 60))
    corpus.append(pem)
    corpus.append(der_prefix)

    # Keep individual entries reasonable
    trimmed = []
    for blob in corpus:
        if len(blob) > 1024:
            trimmed.append(blob[:1024])
        else:
            trimmed.append(blob)
    return trimmed

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    corpus = _assemble_corpus(rng)
    # Pick an entry and return it directly. These are valid inputs for various FUZZ_PARAM_STR sites.
    choice = rng.choice(corpus)
    # Ensure overall size bound
    return bytes(choice[:4096])

# This generator creates plausible numeric strings for Botan's big integer parsers
# used by botan_mp_set_from_str and botan_mp_set_from_radix_str.
# It focuses on valid decimal and hexadecimal forms, sometimes with 0x prefix,
# optional leading sign, leading/trailing zeros, and varied lengths. It may also
# include edge cases like very large numbers, minimal numbers, and boundary sizes.

HEX_DIGITS = "0123456789abcdefABCDEF"
DEC_DIGITS = string.digits

def _rand_decimal(rng: random.Random, max_len: int) -> str:
    # Optional sign
    sign = rng.choice(["", "+", "-"])
    # Avoid empty after sign: ensure at least one digit
    length = rng.randint(1, max_len)
    # Control leading zeros and digit distribution
    if rng.random() < 0.4:
        # Many leading zeros
        lead_zeros = rng.randint(0, max(0, length - 1))
        core_len = max(1, length - lead_zeros)
        core_first = rng.choice("123456789")
        core_rest = "".join(rng.choices(DEC_DIGITS, k=core_len - 1))
        body = ("0" * lead_zeros) + core_first + core_rest
    else:
        # Typical decimal with non-zero first unless single digit
        if length == 1:
            body = rng.choice(DEC_DIGITS)
        else:
            first = rng.choice("123456789")
            rest = "".join(rng.choices(DEC_DIGITS, k=length - 1))
            body = first + rest
    return sign + body

def _rand_hex_body(rng: random.Random, length: int) -> str:
    # Ensure at least one hex digit
    if length <= 0:
        length = 1
    # Control leading zeros probability
    if rng.random() < 0.4 and length > 1:
        lead_zeros = rng.randint(0, length - 1)
        core_len = length - lead_zeros
        core_first = rng.choice("123456789abcdefABCDEF")
        core_rest = "".join(rng.choices(HEX_DIGITS, k=core_len - 1))
        return ("0" * lead_zeros) + core_first + core_rest
    else:
        return "".join(rng.choices(HEX_DIGITS, k=length))

def _rand_hex(rng: random.Random, max_len: int, allow_prefix: bool) -> str:
    sign = rng.choice(["", "+", "-"])
    length = rng.randint(1, max_len)
    body = _rand_hex_body(rng, length)
    prefix = "0x" if (allow_prefix and rng.random() < 0.6) else ""
    return sign + prefix + body

def _edge_cases() -> List[str]:
    # Interesting numeric strings for both decimal and hex contexts
    return [
        "0",
        "+0",
        "-0",
        "00",
        "0000000000000000",
        "1",
        "9",
        "10",
        "42",
        "1234567890",
        "-1",
        "+1",
        "18446744073709551615",  # 2^64-1
        "340282366920938463463374607431768211455",  # 2^128-1
        "115792089237316195423570985008687907853269984665640564039457584007913129639935",  # 2^256-1
        "0x0",
        "+0x0",
        "-0x0",
        "0x1",
        "0xdeadBEEF",
        "0xFFFFFFFF",
        "0xffffffffffffffff",
        "0x7fffffffffffffff",
        "0x100000000",
        "0x1234567890abcdef",
        "+0xABCDEF",
        "-0xABCDEF",
    ]

def _compose_mixed_set(rng: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    items: List[str] = []
    items.extend(_edge_cases())

    # Add a few random decimals and hex numbers of various sizes
    for _ in range(rng.randint(5, 10)):
        items.append(_rand_decimal(rng, max_len=rng.randint(1, 64)))
    for _ in range(rng.randint(5, 10)):
        items.append(_rand_hex(rng, max_len=rng.randint(1, 64), allow_prefix=True))

    # Boundary near 128 bytes (fuzzer trims to 128 chars). Create long numbers.
    # Aim for 120-128 chars including optional sign/prefix.
    target_len = rng.randint(120, 128)
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        # Long decimal
        sign = rng.choice(["", "+", "-"])
        first = rng.choice("123456789")
        rest_len = max(0, target_len - len(sign) - 1)
        rest = "".join(rng.choices(DEC_DIGITS, k=rest_len))
        items.append(sign + first + rest)
    else:
        # Long hex, with optional prefix
        sign = rng.choice(["", "+", "-"])
        prefix = "0x" if rng.random() < 0.6 else ""
        body_len = max(1, target_len - len(sign) - len(prefix))
        items.append(sign + prefix + _rand_hex_body(rng, body_len))

    # Numbers that are powers of two minus one to exercise carry/word boundaries
    for bits in [31, 32, 63, 64, 127, 128, 255, 256, 521]:
        if rng.random() < 0.9:
            # Add decimal representation
            val = (1 << bits) - 1
            items.append(str(val))
            # Add hex representation with prefix
            hex_str = hex(val)
            items.append(hex_str)

    return items

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Decide which target form to emphasize: decimal, hex (with/without 0x), or pick from set
    mode = rng.choice(["decimal", "hex_pref", "hex_nopref", "mixed"])    

    if mode == "mixed":
        options = _compose_mixed_set(rng)
        s = rng.choice(options)
    elif mode == "decimal":
        # Generate a realistic decimal up to 128 characters
        s = _rand_decimal(rng, max_len=rng.randint(1, 120))
    elif mode == "hex_pref":
        s = _rand_hex(rng, max_len=rng.randint(1, 120), allow_prefix=True)
    else:  # hex_nopref
        s = _rand_hex(rng, max_len=rng.randint(1, 120), allow_prefix=False)

    # Ensure total length within the 4096 byte cap (well below due to 128 typical)
    if len(s) > 4096:
        s = s[:4096]

    return s.encode("ascii")

from typing import List

# Generates interesting, mostly-valid bcrypt hash strings and matching/mismatching passwords.
# Target stub calls:
#   pass = FUZZ_PARAM_STR();
#   hash = FUZZ_PARAM_STR();
# and then botan_bcrypt_is_valid(pass.c_str(), hash.c_str());
# So we return a single bytes buffer that, when split by the fuzzing harness, feeds both calls.
# We assume the harness can take our buffer as a corpus entry and split it (e.g., newline) into two FUZZ_PARAM_STRs.
# We therefore encode: password\nhash
# The hash is NUL-terminated implicitly by C-string rules, but we just provide ASCII without embedded NULs.

B64_BCRYPT_ALPHABET = b"ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789+/".replace(b"+", b".")
# Bcrypt uses ./A-Za-z0-9 alphabet; the above produces correct alphabet by replacing '+' with '.' and removing '/'
BCRYPT_ALPHABET = b"ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789./"

# bcrypt hash components
# Format: $2a$cc$22-char-salt22$31-char-hash31 (without extra $ before hash; actual format is $2b$cc$22salt31hash)
# Canonical: $2a$<cost>$<22 chars of ./A-Za-z0-9><31 chars of ./A-Za-z0-9>
# Variants: 2a, 2b, 2y, 2x
VARIANTS = ["2a", "2b", "2y", "2x"]


def _rand_cost(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Typical valid range 04..31
    if rng.random() < 0.85:
        cost = rng.randint(4, 31)
    else:
        # sometimes pick edge or odd values (still in range 04..31)
        choices = [4, 5, 10, 12, 14, 31]
        cost = rng.choice(choices)
    return f"{cost:02d}"


def _rand_bcrypt_str_bytes(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # 22-char salt, 31-char hash from alphabet
    salt = bytes(rng.choice(BCRYPT_ALPHABET) for _ in range(22))
    hsh = bytes(rng.choice(BCRYPT_ALPHABET) for _ in range(31))
    variant = rng.choice(VARIANTS)
    cost = _rand_cost(rng)
    return f"${variant}${cost}$".encode() + salt + hsh


def _rand_password(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Diverse passwords: sometimes empty, sometimes long, with unicode
    modes = rng.random()
    if modes < 0.1:
        return ""  # empty
    elif modes < 0.2:
        return "password"
    elif modes < 0.35:
        return "correct horse battery staple"
    elif modes < 0.5:
        return "Tr0ub4dor&3"
    elif modes < 0.65:
        # include some non-ASCII (though bcrypt typically treats bytes; Botan may accept UTF-8)
        return "pässwörd–测试"
    elif modes < 0.8:
        # long
        return ("A" * rng.randint(1, 64))
    else:
        # random mix
        chars = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + string.punctuation + " \t"
        length = rng.randint(1, 72)  # common bcrypt input length limit
        return "".join(rng.choice(chars) for _ in range(length))


def _make_valid_pair(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # We cannot compute a real bcrypt hash without the algorithm; instead, generate plausible valid format hash strings.
    # Some will purposely match/mismatch password content markers in salt to diversify behavior, though verification will fail.
    pwd = _rand_password(rng).encode("utf-8")
    bch = _rand_bcrypt_str_bytes(rng)
    return pwd + b"\n" + bch


def _make_edge_cases(rng: random.Random) -> List[bytes]:
    out = []
    # Minimal cost, different versions
    for v in ["2a", "2b", "2y", "2x"]:
        salt = BCRYPT_ALPHABET[0:1] * 22
        hsh = BCRYPT_ALPHABET[-1:] * 31
        out.append(bf := (b"edge\n$" + v.encode() + b"$04$" + salt + hsh))
    # Max cost
    salt = BCRYPT_ALPHABET[-2:-1] * 22
    hsh = BCRYPT_ALPHABET[1:2] * 31
    out.append(b"password\n$2b$31$" + salt + hsh)
    # Typical cost 10
    out.append(b"hunter2\n$2a$10$" + (b"./" * 11) + (b"Az" * 15 + b"A"))
    # Empty password with valid-looking hash
    out.append(b"\n" + _rand_bcrypt_str_bytes(rng))
    return out


def _maybe_malformed(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Sometimes generate intentionally malformed formats to drive failure paths
    choice = rng.randint(0, 4)
    if choice == 0:
        # Bad prefix
        salt = b"A" * 22
        hsh = b"B" * 31
        return b"bad\n$9z$10$" + salt + hsh
    if choice == 1:
        # Missing cost
        return b"pass\n$2b$$" + (b"C" * 22) + (b"D" * 31)
    if choice == 2:
        # Short salt
        return b"x\n$2a$12$" + (b"E" * 10) + (b"F" * 31)
    if choice == 3:
        # Short hash
        return b"y\n$2y$12$" + (b"G" * 22) + (b"H" * 10)
    # Non-bcrypt characters in salt/hash
    return b"z\n$2b$12$" + (b"!" * 22) + (b"?" * 31)


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Choose a strategy mix: mostly valid-looking, sometimes malformed for negative paths.
    roll = rng.random()
    if roll < 0.6:
        buf = _make_valid_pair(rng)
    elif roll < 0.85:
        # pick from prepared edge cases
        cases = _make_edge_cases(rng)
        buf = rng.choice(cases)
    else:
        buf = _maybe_malformed(rng)

    # Ensure size limit
    return buf[:4096]
